name: TOTAL (Cincom)
tagline: Cincom's 1968 network-model DBMS, the first sold independently of a hardware vendor; long retired.
description: TOTAL was the first product of Cincom Systems, founded in 1968, and is widely cited as the first commercial database management system sold separately from a computer manufacturer's hardware and software. It used a network (CODASYL-style) model of master and variable record files linked by chains, accessed through a call interface from COBOL and assembler programs on IBM mainframes and other platforms, and became one of the most widely installed DBMSs of the 1970s. Cincom no longer markets TOTAL; its current mainframe database line is sold under the SUPRA name, and Cincom itself was acquired by PartnerOne in 2024.
statusNote: No longer marketed by Cincom, whose mainframe database products are now sold as SUPRA (PDM and SQL); Cincom was acquired by PartnerOne in 2024.
strengths: Pioneered the independent DBMS software market in the late 1960s
Simple master/variable file network model was efficient on small mainframes
weaknesses: Navigational access only: programs walk record chains instead of declaring queries
Long out of the market; skills and documentation are scarce
